task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: How is 'role travels' defined and measured (stability of play-type shares, or of the initiator role, before and after a team change)?
Can a comparison between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers be powered with n=24 units?
How can role persistence be separated from teammate, coach, system and landing-spot confounding?
How reliable are play-by-play-derived CUT and DRIVE labels and initiator attribution?
How much do regression to the mean and selection on the classification period distort portability?

historical_evidence.finding: Destination net-rating checks for movers (portability vs destination net rating change) were recorded as 'underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality'. [prior work] lists failure mechanism A_unanswerable, limits low power/large MDE and small sample, and risk SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER. The sample and power were not recorded. It was dropped from Paper 1.

Player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap for initiators: mean gap +0.427 PPP, in the same direction as the team-level gap. Only 3 players cleared n>=30 in both tiers, and most star cells were below the n>=30 gate ([prior work], RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER). This concerns a different question.

Play-type PPP across playoff series game buckets: DRIVE 0.889 to 0.949 (+0.060) and CUT +0.114, with 'no clear signal'. [prior work] is observational, has no CIs, and carries a selection/regression-to-the-mean limitation.
Descriptive tabulation of how often trigger possessions land on BEST vs AVOID counters, by team and player. Player samples ranged from 10 to 178 possessions. There was no outcome test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing mover portability against destination on-court net rating, including origin-to-destination change.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: low power with a large MDE and small sample. The result was null once corrected for landing-spot quality, and it was dropped from Paper 1.

evidence_establishes: An earlier project attempt to study mover portability with a destination-outcome measure was recorded as untestable, because of low power and sample size and a landing-spot-quality confound ([prior work][prior work]).
Player-level play-type analyses in this project repeatedly hit small per-player possession counts ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Nothing retrieved tests whether cut-heavy shapers' roles are more stable across team changes than drive-heavy shapers' roles.
No retrieved record defines or validates a 'shaper' classification or a role-portability metric based on play-type shares.
[prior work] do not show whether CUT and DRIVE labels derived from play-by-play are reliable for individual players.
The sample size, power and MDE of [prior work][prior work] were not recorded, so its power cannot be compared with this study's.
[prior work] do not show whether a role-stability (rather than net-rating) outcome would avoid the landing-spot confound.
own_inferences: n=24 split into two profile groups (about 12 each) detects only very large differences (roughly d>=1.2 at 80% power for a two-group comparison, or |r|>=0.55 for a continuous cut-share moderator). A modest advantage for cut-heavy shapers would be undetectable.
The most likely result of a competent test is inconclusive or untestable, not a clean support or rejection.
Cut-heavy players are often finishers or off-ball players whose cut share depends on teammates and the offensive system, so cut share may not travel regardless of the underlying role.

Selecting players as extreme cut-heavy or drive-heavy on pre-move data invites regression to the mean in post-move shares, and this could differ by group because the two shares have different base rates and noise.
Because the claim is vague ('travel better', 'shapers'), flexible operationalisation could produce a spurious support finding unless the definitions are fixed in advance.
uncertainties: The 'shaper' definition is not given in the task statement or the retrieved records; I did not call the glossary.
It is unknown whether the 24 units are players, player-moves or player-seasons, and whether some players appear more than once.
Post-move possession counts per player are unknown, which determines how reliable each portability measure is.
It is unknown how many of the 24 units are cut-heavy vs drive-heavy.
[prior work][prior work], listed as related to [prior work][prior work], was not read, so I do not know what it contains.
Data for 2025-26 may still be partial for some moves.

historical_effect.explanation: The directly relevant record ([prior work][prior work], untestable, underpowered, dropped) and the repeated small-sample limits in the other records made me move from a tentative 'proceed with changes' to 'do_not_proceed' for a confirmatory test. I recommend only a pre-specified descriptive/estimation analysis.
